gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-devanagar: Powerful and ancient, Nordic spaces its letters like brush dabs set far apart, with a cramped, folded look inside each one. Noto Sans Devanagari follows with an open lower curve on its g and a compact skyline, so the heading feels carved and the text feels modern.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-duployan:
Noto Sans Duployan has a wide-mouthed a and oversized counters.

Nordic sits above it, closed up and monoweight, so the heading feels pressed tight while the sans-serif text below opens out and lets the lines breathe.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Blunt, brushy and old-feeling, Nordic holds one unvarying weight from word to word, with gaps between letters like dabs of ink. Noto Sans Elbasan is the opposite: large, open and clear.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic:
Noto Sans Ethiopic is sturdy and tall, with terminals hanging far from the bowl.

Over a long passage it would read steadily and openly, a relief after Nordic's flat, unvarying strokes and its tightly closed letters.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Tight, ancient and flat-stroked, Nordic leads with essentially zero stroke contrast and closed-up letters. Noto Sans Georgian takes over below with open curves and short ascender stems, making the whole page feel modern and clean.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-glagoliti:
Nordic hits hard, with brush-dab spacing and matching strokes.

Its best trick is that weighty, ancient presence, while Noto Sans Glagolitic does the quieter job of staying clear and approachable with open, round letters and sturdy, tall lowercase bodies.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic reads wide open, its lowercase counters as large as drilled glass beads and its rounds like open parentheses. Nordic, by contrast, looks cut from wire and closed tight, and a larger size for it would let that heading hold its own.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-grantha:
Noto Sans Grantha has tall, pen-nib bowls pressed flat, so the eye never snags on a closed-up shape.

Nordic, with its powerful, ancient monoweight strokes, is a hard heading to follow, yet Noto Sans Grantha keeps the reading smooth and plain.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-gujarati:
Noto Sans Gujarati has curved strokes that stop before turning inward.

Nordic does the heavy lifting up top with stems like dowels and arcs like bent dowels, while the sans-serif body simply stays clean and open in its tall, large-countered letters.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-g: Contemporary and crisp, Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi cuts its terminals back to leave big gaps, with strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark. Nordic's stylus-at-fixed-pressure line is its opposite, so a long passage would read lightly under a heavy, closed heading.
